Read transcript 345–640s and catalogue chapters: this lies within Cross Entropy Loss (194–845), with English auto captions and embed availability. At 375.13–400.22 the speaker starts a PyTorch criterion setup. At 411.14–431.24 he correctly explains internal log-softmax plus NLL and not applying softmax to input logits. BLOCKING accuracy defect: at 431.24–446.54 he states that Y 'must not be one hot encoded' and one 'should only put the correct class label', without restricting this assertion to the class-index target contract. Current approved CrossEntropyLoss documentation explicitly supports either class indices or floating class-probability targets of the same shape as logits; valid floating one-hot distributions are included. This 2020 blanket restriction is obsolete. At 459.29–533.99 he creates class-zero targets and a one-by-three raw-score prediction, then a worse prediction. At 555.44–610.70 he calls the criterion on both and shows the good prediction has lower loss; this does substantively teach f1. BLOCKING coverage overclaim: f2's long dtype, general target shape (N,), and valid target interval are not taught, so f2 is not confirmed. Narrated tensor edits, slide references, calls and execution suggest live-code/slides rather than a pure talking head, though frames were not directly inspected. No later concept is needed. A contiguous tightened cut cannot keep criterion setup and the complete demo while removing the inaccurate intervening target rule; a new accurate standalone source/range is needed. Merely label-matching this as a class-index example does not amend what the speaker says.

Read transcript 149–578s and catalogue chapters: Lazy Method 180–320 and Recommended Method 320 onward; English captions and embed availability. At 179.91–206.10 a small model and filename are introduced. At 206.10–218.54 torch.save(model,file) writes the whole object; 262.56–286.26 restores it with bare torch.load(file), then eval. BLOCKING modern-API accuracy defect: the whole-module reload is presented as immediately executable, but current approved saveloadrun documentation uses weights_only=False for this legacy pickle case, explicitly contrasting weights_only=True for weight loading. I also opened https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/generated/torch.load.html: its signature explicitly defaults weights_only=True and its parameter description restricts the loader to tensors, primitive types, dictionaries and allowlisted types. Under this weights-only default, this bare whole-model call fails for an ordinary custom Module. Do not publish this as an unchanged modern demo or silently assume an older environment; choose a current weights-only demo or explicitly version-bound source. At 320.31–386.70 he switches to saving state_dict. At 390.14–439.80 he constructs the matching model with six inputs, loads the mapping via load_state_dict(torch.load(file)), and calls eval. At 452.64–491.22 he explicitly says no training occurred and visually compares the random initialized weight/bias tensors, then at 509.76–548.20 shows state_dict's weight and bias entries. These teach the f1 persistence/compatible-architecture mechanism and f3, not f2's explicit weights_only=True, fixture predictions, assertions or quantitative comparisons. Saving untrained parameter state is a legitimate demonstration of the same persistence mechanism, not evidence of trained predictions. Code edits, script runs, explorer/file inspection and printed tensors support live-code visual value; no frames directly reviewed. No blocked device-placement lesson occurs before 548. The 369s duration is partly consumed by the obsolete whole-object alternative. Tightening to 320 would discard the only introduction of the model/filename used in the demo, leaving an unresolved setup dependency; select another self-contained accurate range rather than approving that cut. The checkpoint/optimizer extension beginning 548.20 is outside the proposal.
